clue.text: Being first, moving quickly across border

indicators.note: the speedy word lies across the edge word, holding it in its middle

parts.note: pacy is an informal word for fast
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone races over a frontier to get ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being first' reads like a race result, but it is a noun phrase meaning supremacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Primacy is the state of coming first in rank or importance.

clue.text: Engineers let loose

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A team of engineers are set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is a verb here, meaning to set free, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to free it, as one frees a captive.

clue.text: Wise man from university featured in publications

indicators.note: a story featured in magazines appears inside them

parts.note: mags are magazines

explanation.surface: A sage from a university gets written up in magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a sage or learned magician, like the Magi of the Nativity.

clue.text: Small firm supports unoriginal types

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, a firm
piers are pillars that hold up a structure

explanation.surface: A little company backs people who never come up with their own ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Copiers imitate others' work, so they lack originality.

clue.text: State in which a non-Christian priest entertains a bishop?

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so the priest word holds the other letters

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A US state where a Buddhist cleric plays host to a Christian bishop, perhaps an unlikely scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an unlikely scene of a lama hosting a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Harry gets praise — along with Harry's granny

parts.note: to laud is to praise
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, grandmother of Prince Harry

explanation.surface: A man named Harry is praised, and so is his grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music hall singer, so 'Harry' defines his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauder is the surname of the music hall star whose first name was Harry.

clue.text: Dead growth removed maybe? Diversify

definitions.meaning: a withered limb of a tree pruned away

explanation.surface: A gardener prunes dead wood, then decides to try something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a dead branch taken out of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Branching out means extending into new areas, and literally a limb that has been cut off.

clue.text: Set out to the south of island for fish

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece south of another sits below it

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: the letters of set are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Nets cast south of an island to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullets are a family of edible sea fish, red and grey.

clue.text: What would be very holy in hell?

definitions.text: What would be very holy in hell?

parts.words: What would be very holy in hell?
parts.note: the abyss of hell is endless, so 'very holy' plays on holey; and the pit with its bottom letter gone leaves PI, slang for very pious

explanation.walkthrough: PI is slang for pious; PIT with its last letter removed gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abyss of hell is described in the Bible as a pit with no floor.

clue.text: Hit record following Sinatra's number one

indicators.note: the record word comes after the initial, so it is placed second
the first letter of the singer's name is its number one, its leading letter

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A hit record that came after Sinatra's chart-topper.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog a ball is to hit it hard and wildly, as in cricket.

clue.text: One paid, possibly responsive to treatment on offer?

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is someone paid for what they do
a curable illness may respond to medical treatment

explanation.surface: A paid professional who might be cured, offered up for business.
explanation.definitionFit: Something procurable can be obtained, so it is available or on offer.

clue.text: Bother one thus to become Man, for instance

indicators.note: the clue tells us how the answer must be changed to turn into the island word, so we work back from it

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grumble about the trouble of becoming a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: replace HAS in the answer with I (one) and it becomes ISLE, as in the Isle of Man. Bloggers found the instruction loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother and hassle are both nouns or verbs for annoying trouble or pestering.

clue.text: Plate of food? One may dig in

definitions.meaning: an old wooden board or platter for serving food
someone who cuts trenches, a digger

explanation.surface: A dish arrives and someone tucks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dig in' suggests eating, playing on the plate, but here it means digging trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is an old serving board for food, and also anyone who digs trenches.

clue.text: Dull clothes is in for some East Enders

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
at home means in, and Cockneys of London's East End drop the H, saying 'ome

explanation.surface: Drab clothing is in fashion among Londoners in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders are Cockneys from East London, who drop the H of home.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiresome, tedious and dull.

clue.text: More than one old vagabond manages to pinch precious material

indicators.note: the managing word grips the gem word between its letters

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
agate is a semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: Old tramps succeed in stealing something valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer or fugitive.

clue.text: American student goes round America with a particular musical instrument

indicators.note: the student word surrounds the country letters

parts.note: a soph is a sophomore, a second-year student in the US
USA is short for the United States of America
one as in 'one day', meaning a particular day

explanation.surface: An American student tours the country carrying a special musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sousaphone is a large brass tuba designed to wrap around a marching player.

clue.text: See 16
Game shot in this place where cattle may graze?

indicators.note: the shot game is placed in the word for this place

parts.note: here means in this place
a bag is the quantity of game shot by a hunter

explanation.surface: Hunters shoot game on the very land where cows feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and herbs, pasture for livestock.

clue.text: Raises poultry, having brought in crew?

indicators.note: the poultry word takes in the crew word inside itself

parts.note: hens are poultry
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone farms chickens after hiring some workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises' looks like rearing poultry, but it means lifts.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten something is to raise or intensify it.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about tirade one's receiving

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the tirade word

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: Someone getting something exclaims in surprise at a rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grantee is a recipient of a grant, one who gets it.

clue.text: One lacking love and pain, sitting in a home

indicators.note: the word one goes without the letter for love

parts.note: O is love, nil in tennis
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone unloved and hurting sits at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the O (love) from ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting describes a bird sitting in its nest.

clue.text: Female not so young — one getting creases

parts.note: older means less young

explanation.surface: An ageing woman starts to get wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: The creases suggest a lined face, but they are folds in paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder is a person or machine that folds paper, putting creases in it.

clue.text: Old soldiers move slowly, soon with leader falling behind

parts.note: to drag is to move slowly and heavily

indicators.note: the first letter of the word soon drops back to the end

explanation.surface: Veteran troops trudge along, with their commander soon lagging at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader falling behind' moves the S of SOON to the end, making OONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragoons were mounted infantry in historic armies.

clue.text: Lover deprived of maiden becomes tense

indicators.note: something deprived of a thing has it taken away

parts.note: an amorist is a lover
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A lover denied a young woman becomes anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' reads as the adjective anxious but is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorist is a past tense in Greek grammar.

clue.text: Tries with difficulty to become a candidate once more

definitions.text: to become a candidate once more

indicators.note: letters handled with difficulty are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A student struggles to take the exam again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination again after failing.

clue.text: Maybe acts as the ancient mariner?

parts.note: a word ..., its letters set loose, could become acts, so acts is an example of what the phrase gives

explanation.surface: Someone performs in the role of Coleridge's old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read the answer as wordplay, ADRIFT as the anagram signal on CAST, and it yields 'acts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's mariner drifts lost at sea, like a sailor set loose in a boat.

clue.text: Muslim greeting received by religious charity

indicators.note: the charity takes in the greeting, holding it inside

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian charity
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A Muslim's hello is welcomed by a faith-based charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Shia is one of the two main branches of Islam, also used for a member.

clue.text: This person has a certain degree

parts.note: me is how a speaker or setter refers to themself
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of holding a particular qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Measure and degree both mean extent or amount, as in 'a measure of success'.

clue.text: Number time and time again in temporary accommodation?

parts.note: ten is a number
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A count repeated again and again in a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentage is tents collectively, shelter used for short stays.
